newsitem.title: DENMARK: East Asiatic sells off German meat plant.
newsitem.headline: East Asiatic sells off German meat plant.

text.p: Denmark's East Asiatic Company (EAC) said on Monday its German subsidiary Plumrose Deutschland had reached final agreement on the sale of its loss-making Britz German meat processing plant near Berlin.

The sale, already announced provisionally on December 30, 1996, was to Gerhard Thien, owner of Fuerstenberger Fleischwaren GmbH, a meat processing plant 150 km from Britz with a 150 million crown annual turnover, it said.
EAC said the purchaser had satisfied all financing conditions and that the deal was now finalised, backdated to January 1, 1997.

The Britz plant and two other German sites producing EAC's Plumrose brand have long been a drag on their parent company, draining 300 million crowns over the past two years, with a provision for 150 million crowns more, EAC said last July.
According to EAC CEO Michael Fiorini then, it had originally hoped to sell all three plants as a package, but would probably have to retain Boeklund and Edewecht for the time being.
Britz had been responsible for the lion's share of the losses and keeping the other two until a suitable buyer appeared would not be a significant burden, he said.
